claim_being_audited: That rejecting Kestrel-Borderline-018 was policy-compliant and adequately supported by admissible evidence because unresolved due-diligence risks meant the vendor was not approvable on the record at decision time.
specific_concerns: The cited evidence shows an informal undocumented quality process and an unresolved questionnaire variance, but the policy states those facts justify follow-up or escalation and do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure.
The packet overreaches from 'not cleared for approval yet' to 'reject_vendor' without an admissible link showing the unresolved issues were materially disqualifying rather than pending remediation.
No admissible evidence shows a failed control test, formal security finding, or other logged basis elevating the issues from diligence gaps to rejection-level risk.
The actor's own summary concedes the admissible case for outright rejection is limited and weaker than a case for follow-up or escalation.
unsupported_claims: That the available admissible record is sufficient to support outright vendor rejection rather than deferral, follow-up, or escalation.
That the unresolved diligence issues, as documented, amount to a material reject-level control failure.
That 'vendor was not cleared for approval' is equivalent to 'reject_vendor' under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: A formally logged finding showing the storage-control variance was material and unresolved at decision time.
Any admissible materiality assessment or approval matrix showing that the cited quality-process and storage issues require rejection rather than follow-up.
Any logged failed control test, formal review outcome, or procurement rule that makes this combination of issues disqualifying.
decision_criteria: Rejecting a vendor requires admissible due-diligence evidence of a material unresolved risk.
Quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies alone support follow-up or escalation, not reject-level failure.
Private or unlogged security-review conclusions cannot be cited or inferred into the record.
A compliant rejection needs a clear evidentiary bridge from observed diligence gaps to a policy-recognized rejection threshold.
